title: ENOSPC on a run-directory write triggers garbage collection and the run resumes
proves: writeNode's write goes through writeRunTextWithDiskPressureRetry (disk-gc.mjs): a write that fails with ENOSPC runs garbage collection once and retries, and the retry succeeds once GC has reclaimed enough space. A finished, unlocked, older run sitting under .runs/ is exactly the kind of directory GC may reclaim, and with INTENT_FACTORY_SIMULATE_GC_ROUNDS bounding the deterministic threshold stand-in to exactly the one candidate available, GC removes precisely that old run and logs it to gc.jsonl with reason enospc — never more than the minimum necessary. The two guards that matter most hold throughout: the run currently writing (d09-run) is never a GC candidate, and .runs/campaigns/, the durable handoff, is never even considered. The node itself completes normally (status done, one worker invocation, no routing hop recorded), since the retry-after-GC path is not a failover edge.

contract.goal: prove ENOSPC on a run-directory write triggers garbage collection once and the write resumes
